agent_notes: Reviewer request applied: the commentary now says todah comes back in verse 4 only (betodah), with its root again in hodu in the same verse; verse 3 has no todah.

The superscription 'mizmor letodah' is verse 1 in the Hebrew numbering; the KJV counts it as verse 0 and starts its verse 1 at 'Make a joyful noise'. The verse map handles this; the commentary mentions it in one sentence.
KJV 'Psalm of praise' translates letodah, which is thanksgiving (todah), not praise (tehillah). Corrected in the literal layer; YLT and ASV agree with 'thanksgiving'.

Glossed הָרִיעוּ as 'shout in acclamation' rather than STEPBible's 'shout for joy': the root ruaʿ is the war-cry and the trumpet blast with which a king is acclaimed. The Malbim passage in the packet (quoting Ps 47:2) supports this reading; the lexicon nuance (BDB) is my own recollection and not cited.

agent_notes: Ketiv/Qere: written וְלֹא ('and not'), read וְלוֹ ('and to him'). The packet's tokens carry the reading. The KJV follows the Ketiv ('and not we ourselves'); ASV, YLT and BBE follow the Qere ('and we are his'). I follow the Qere in all layers and give the Ketiv in the note and commentary. Radak and Meiri in the packet discuss the Ketiv; Ibn Ezra notes the Gaon's variant reading.
The STEPBible entity tag deity.yhwh on אֱלֹהִים is correct here; the word has a plural form but takes singular predicates (hu', ʿasanu).

Whether 'amo / we-tzon' is a second predicate ('we are his people') or an apposition to the object ('his people, the flock of his pasture') is not settled by the text; I render it as a clause with 'we are' carried over from the previous phrase, following the translations unanimously.

Синодальный перевод (Пс 99:1) озаглавливает псалом «Псалом хвалебный» и включает заголовок в стих 1: «Псалом хвалебный. Воскликните Господу, вся земля!». Комментарий приводит именно эту цитату; про нумерацию сказано только то, что в еврейском счёте заголовок входит в стих 1, а KJV считает его стихом 0.
В буквальном слое глагол הריעו передан как «воскликните в ликовании», чтобы сохранить оттенок радостного клича (корень рууа‘); YHWH оставлено, как в английском буквальном слое.
